solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cabbage served by short bloke with hair in a tangle

indicators.note: letters in a tangle are mixed up, so these are rearranged
short tells us to cut the last letter off the word bloke

explanation.surface: A stubby man with messy hair serves up cabbage at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims BLOKE to BLOK; with HAIR that makes BLOKHAIR, which 'in a tangle' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is a turnip-like variety of the brassica family, so cabbage stands for it.

clue.text: Dispatch, briefly, chap where cats traditionally fought?

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to dispatch someone is to kill them
Kenny is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A chap is sent off, briefly, to the place famed for feline fights.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kilkenny cats of the Irish rhyme fought until only their tails were left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish town gives its name to the legendary pair of cats that fought to mutual destruction.

clue.text: Gang locked up in Norwich or Derby

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words Norwich or Derby, spanning them

explanation.surface: A criminal gang is jailed in one of two English cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang and a horde are both large groups of people, often unruly.

clue.text: Lawrence can marry Dot, surprisingly, in the old county

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the assumed name Ross

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected rearrangement of the words can marry Dot

explanation.surface: A man called Lawrence can wed a woman named Dot, to everyone's surprise, in an old county.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia joined the RAF as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a historic Scottish county in the Highlands, abolished in 1975, hence old.

clue.text: Persecutor repressing most of family in massive way

indicators.note: repressing means holding down, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a bully persecutes the weak

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter of the word for family

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A tormentor crushes most of a family in a big, heavy way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting bulkily means doing so in a large, heavy-bodied, massive manner.

clue.text: Gangster with sons in Paris that give the game away

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
que is French for that
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster and his boys in Paris let slip what they are up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal is slang for informing, betraying a secret to police or rivals.

clue.text: One risking knockout given big drink reported a better roll

parts.note: a quart is two pints, a large drink

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a better roll is a finer list, a roll being a list of names

explanation.surface: A boxer facing a knockout downs a big drink and is said to have a stronger record.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a finer list' sounds like the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the last eight of a knockout tournament risks elimination in the next round.

clue.text: Bird fish in European river avoid

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
to duck something is to dodge or avoid it

explanation.surface: A fish in a European river tries to dodge something.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its soft down feathers, a type of bird.

clue.text: Way to cut turnover of proper food store

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so one piece goes inside the other
turnover of means the word for proper is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: real means genuine, proper
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A route through a proper financial turnover sounds like business planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover of' reverses REAL to LAER, which RD cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cool room where provisions are kept is a store for food.

clue.text: Stab of pain, note, restricting footballer

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the note encloses the footballer

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a wing is a player on the flank of a football team

explanation.surface: A sharp pain is noted, keeping a footballer out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp brief pain is a stab, a pang.

clue.text: Primate in sporting venue, one standing in for duke

indicators.note: standing in for means replacing, so one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monkey at a sports ground stands in for a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground; swapping its D for I gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This slow-moving nocturnal animal of southern Asia is a primate related to lemurs.

clue.text: Cow maybe crossing loch with a native of Ayrshire, perhaps

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece straddles the other

parts.note: a cow is something that lows, so playfully a lower
L is the abbreviation for loch or lake
and means with, in addition to

explanation.surface: A cow wades across a Scottish loch alongside an Ayrshire farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow maybe' is a whimsical lower, a thing that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrshire lies in the Scottish Lowlands, so its people are examples of Lowland Scots.

clue.text: Promotion of English verse welcomed in great joy

indicators.note: welcomed in means taken inside, so the joy holds the two letters

parts.note: elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A rise up the ranks for English poetry is greeted with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank or position is a promotion.

clue.text: Brusque ambassador abandoning the Irish language

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so letters are taken out of the phrase

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Irish Gaelic
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A curt diplomat gives up speaking Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency, an ambassador) leaves THE ERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech that is short and abrupt to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: Time old working lawyer employed in city

indicators.note: employed in means placed inside, so these go within the city

parts.note: NY is New York
on means functioning, working
DA is District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: An elderly lawyer still at work is busy in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular time of day.

clue.text: Where some were once confined, changing to blue tie

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters in to blue tie

explanation.surface: Someone is changing into a blue tie, perhaps at a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor, where prisoners were left.

clue.text: Reprimand makes student finally leave weeping

indicators.note: leave means go away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: tearful means weeping

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of student

explanation.surface: A telling-off leaves a pupil in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'student', T, leaves TEARFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down or long scolding is an informal reprimand.

clue.text: It blows with exceptional fury ultimately around compound

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the outer pieces enclose the compound
ultimately picks the final letter of each of the words exceptional and fury

parts.note: an ester is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: Something gusts with exceptional fury, swirling around a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the west is one that blows across the land.

clue.text: Satellite given award by Reagan, perhaps?

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
Ron, the first name of Ronald Reagan, as an example of a Ron

explanation.surface: Someone receives an honour from an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the moons of Uranus, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Off making case for current whim

indicators.note: making case for means forming a container round the next piece

parts.note: not on means unacceptable, off
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: It is out of order to build an argument for a fleeting fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion can be a sudden fanciful impulse or idea, a whim.

clue.text: Loyal type that is a constructor of courses

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, loyal person

explanation.surface: A faithful person who designs golf courses or race tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: The courses are layers of bricks in a wall, not race or golf courses; a brickie is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer builds walls in rows of bricks called courses.

clue.text: First part of piece initially testing Beecham, for example

parts.note: a bar is a part of a piece of music
one means first

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of testing

explanation.surface: The opening bars of a composition test the conductor Beecham.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Beecham, the conductor, held this hereditary title.
explanation.definitionFit: Beecham inherited this hereditary rank, below a baron, so he is an example.

clue.text: Sign of neglect we found among horse breeders, originally?

indicators.note: found among means placed amid, so the word we sits between the other pieces

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of breeders

explanation.surface: We spot something left untended among horse breeders.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider webs gather in neglected corners, so their presence signals a lack of care.

clue.text: Tranquilliser, one taken with hesitation after work

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the work comes first

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sedative after work, though not without hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: This narcotic from poppies acts as a sedative that calms and dulls the senses.

clue.text: Call a good worker a shrew?

parts.note: to term something is to call it
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Is it fair to call a diligent employee a shrew?
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew in the old sense is a scolding woman, which is what a virago is.

clue.text: Cry of Cockney hunting in part of Clackmannanshire?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: halloa is a cry used in hunting to urge on hounds

explanation.surface: A Londoner shouts while out hunting in a Scottish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunting' places the cry: halloa is the huntsman's call. Clackmannanshire is Scotland's smallest county.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is the main settlement of Clackmannanshire in central Scotland.

clue.text: Curiously narrow, wet, and currently eroded

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters of narrow and wet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange description of a channel that is slim, damp and worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock smoothed by the flow of a stream is worn by water currents.

clue.text: Sort of pulley not working right?

parts.note: idle means not working

explanation.surface: A pulley that doesn't function properly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a pulley or wheel that guides a belt without transmitting power.

clue.text: Informal valediction from a couple of extras

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the word is given twice

parts.note: a bye is one of the extras in cricket, runs not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A casual farewell drawn from a pair of film extras.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the ball touching the bat, counted among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual way to say farewell or goodbye.

clue.text: Art works head removed from river mouth, receiving thanks

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the trimmed word holds the thanks
head removed from means its first letter is taken off

parts.note: an estuary is the wide mouth of a river
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Artworks have been taken from the mouth of a river, with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head removed from' cuts ESTUARY to STUARY, which takes in TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues collectively are works of sculptural art.
